rendered:
Yes, for the first of the panel E sets, labelled Eduardo et al. 2019[1]. The text says the pan-genome analysis revealed 19,469 total genes[2], of which only 3155[3] are core genes (~16.2%[4]). In the pan-genome panel of the figure, the core bar reads contains 3155 genes[5], the dispensable bar contains 7847 genes[6], and the unique bar contains 8467 genes[7]. Their sum is 19,469[8] genes, which matches the stated total. The core share works out to 16.2[9] percent, consistent with the text. The text's citation [44][10] is E. Abreo, N. Altier[11], which appears to be the study behind the first set (an inference from the author name, not stated in the figure).

The other sets in the pan-genome panel do not sum to the text's total, but they come from different studies, so they are not the source of that figure. The Danesh et al. 2016[12] bars sum to 13,587[13] genes, and the Filipe et al. 2018[14] bars sum to 16,456[15] genes. Neither matches the total, so the text's total corresponds only to the first set.
